text:
Buffalo lost 4-0 at home to a Dallas team it out-chanced over the full game. Jake Oettinger stopped all 26 shots he faced, which the model rates at 2.4 goals better than expected, while Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen allowed four on 18 shots, 1.9 goals worse than the chances against him deserved. Buffalo took 63 shot attempts to Dallas's 39 and finished with 2.37 expected goals to 2.10, enough that the BUF side wins 55 percent of simulated replays.

The game turned in a 6:21 stretch of the second period. Sam Steel made it 2-0 at 9:36 on a snap shot the model gave a 5 percent chance. Mikko Rantanen added a 23 percent backhand at 13:57, and Roope Hintz converted the power play at 15:34 for 4-0. Jason Robertson had opened the scoring in the first on a snap shot from Rantanen and Wyatt Johnston. Dallas led the second period 1.20 to 0.59 in expected goals, its one stretch of clear control, and made the most of it. Rantanen finished with a goal and three assists, Johnston three assists, and Hintz a goal on six shots.

Buffalo's best hockey came when the game was already gone. The Sabres led the third period 1.36 to 0.29 in expected goals but had nothing to show for it, with Tage Thompson putting six shots on goal. They went 0 for 3 on the power play while Dallas scored on one of its two chances, and Dallas won 38 of 61 faceoffs. Oettinger's night made that pressure moot.
